ops.title: Export the loaded extension's build identity from _native so hosts need not hash a file
ops.description:
## Why

`prepared_fact_producer` (cc-transcript 14.42.0, #56) must change with every build whose fact extraction or in-memory fact layout could differ. The core has no build identity of its own, so the host supplies one. Captain Hook (yasyf/captain-hook#362) builds it in the owner process as `capt-hook/<Build> cc-transcript/<version> native/sha256:<digest of the file at _native.__file__>`.

That digest is read from the extension's path after the extension is loaded. If the file at that path is replaced between the load and the hash, the owner labels its facts with the new file's digest while running the old code. A later owner that runs the new code then adopts facts the old code extracted. The window is one owner's start, roughly the time from importing cc_transcript to the hello reply. A release install is not exposed: each capt-hook build gets its own tool directory before any owner runs from it. An in-place replacement of an installed extension under a running host is exposed (a same-version development reinstall is the realistic case).

An independent review of #362 rated this a blocker; it was shipped with the limit documented in Captain Hook's changelog, because a sound fix does not exist on the consumer side: Python cannot learn which inode a loaded image came from on macOS without spawning a tool, and hashing before the import needs the owner's startup restructured.

## What to build

`_native` reports the identity of the image that is actually loaded, with no file read at call time. Candidates, in order of preference:

1. The linker's content identity of the image: Mach-O `LC_UUID` on macOS and the GNU build-id note on Linux, read from the loaded image's own headers. Exact, free at run time, and changes with any change to the linked output. Needs a check that the release wheels are linked with a build-id on manylinux.
2. A build script that stamps a digest of every workspace crate's sources and `Cargo.lock` into the binary. Deterministic, but a build script does not re-run when only a dependency crate changes unless it names those paths with `rerun-if-changed`, so the core crate's sources must be listed.

Then the host sends only its own token and the owner appends what `_native` reports. Captain Hook drops `fact_producer`'s file read (about 12 ms per owner start with the file cached).

## Notes

- The producer string's format is the host's business; cc-transcript only compares it. Changing it discards the reuse cache once.
- Captain Hook's dev builds all carry `Build = "0.0.0"`, so on a development host the extension identity is the only part of the string that changes.

ops.text: `_native` exposes a build identity that differs between any two builds whose compiled code differs, and is read without opening the extension file at call time
A test loads the extension, replaces the file at its path with different bytes, and shows the reported identity is still the loaded image's
Captain Hook's owner uses that identity instead of hashing `_native.__file__`, and its changelog drops the 'replace an installed extension only while the host is stopped' caveat
